<challenge>
Design and build the strongest Gmail-inspired email application you can.

Recreate the clarity, information density, speed, and familiar workflows of a great modern inbox. Take the implementation as far as you can: choose the stack, scope, visual direction, data model, and technical limits that let you deliver the most convincing complete product.
</challenge>

<essential-outcomes>
The finished application must include:

- A polished, responsive mail shell with a recognizable inbox, navigation, toolbar, search, and account controls.
- A realistic seeded mailbox with varied senders, subjects, timestamps, labels, read states, attachments, threads, and message content.
- Functional mailbox navigation for at least Inbox, Starred, Sent, Drafts, and Trash.
- Working message selection, read/unread state, starring, archiving, deleting, and labeling.
- A usable search experience that filters or retrieves relevant mail.
- A message-reading view with a clear conversation hierarchy and useful actions.
- A compose experience with recipients, subject, body, draft behavior, send behavior, and a polished interaction model.
- Responsive behavior that remains coherent and usable on both desktop and mobile.
</essential-outcomes>

<product-depth>
Go beyond a static visual recreation. Interactions should update the interface consistently, preserve state where useful, and make the product feel alive. You may add keyboard shortcuts, bulk actions, category tabs, snoozing, scheduled mail, contact suggestions, rich composition, settings, themes, offline persistence, or any other details that strengthen the experience.

No external email account, authentication, paid service, or API key is required. A fully local product with excellent seeded data and convincing behavior is valid. Do not leave prominent controls as decorative placeholders when a meaningful local interaction can be implemented.
</product-depth>

<creative-freedom>
You have broad freedom over architecture, libraries, layout details, interaction design, copy, and visual polish. Use Gmail as the product reference, but make deliberate decisions and deliver a coherent application rather than a collection of disconnected screens.

Do not explain your design before building it. Make the product and engineering decisions yourself, implement the experience, test the important workflows, and refine it into the best result you can.
</creative-freedom>

<success-criteria>
The result should immediately read as a high-quality email client, reward exploration, and support a convincing end-to-end flow from finding a message to reading, organizing, composing, and sending mail. Visual fidelity matters, but functional depth, consistency, responsiveness, and product judgment matter just as much.
</success-criteria>

args.command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
import re
s=open('src/data/seedThreads.ts').read()
blocks=re.split(r"\n  \{\n    id: '", s)[1:]
for b in blocks:
    id_=b.split("'")[0]
    subj=re.search(r"subject: '((?:[^'\\]|\\.)*)'|subject: \"([^\"]*)\"|subject: `([^`]*)`", b)
    cat=re.search(r"category: '(\w+)'", b).group(1)
    loc=re.search(r"location: '(\w+)'", b)
    un='U' if 'unread: true' in b[:400] else ' '
    st='S' if 'starred: true' in b[:400] else ' '
    im='I' if 'important: true' in b[:400] else ' '
    lab=re.search(r"labels: \[([^\]]*)\]", b[:400])
    ats=re.findall(r"at: '([^']+)'", b)
    froms=re.findall(r"from: '([^']+)'", b)
    att=b.count('attachments:')
    htm=b.count('html:')
    print(f"{id_:28} {cat:10} {(loc.group(1) if loc else 'inbox'):8} {un}{st}{im} {lab.group(1) if lab else '':22} n={len(ats)} att={att} html={htm} ats={ats} from={froms} | {(subj.group(1) or subj.group(2) or subj.group(3)) if subj else ''}")
EOF

---
name: portly
description: Manage persistent projects and temporary local processes with the Portly macOS app and CLI. Use when an agent needs to run, start, stop, restart, inspect logs or health, configure projects and ports, adopt external listeners, resolve port conflicts, or enable launch at login.
---

# Portly

Use the `portly` CLI as the primary interface. Every command launches Portly.app automatically if needed; this is a state-changing side effect even for `status` when the app was closed.

If `portly` is not available on `PATH`, use the onboarding-installed CLI at `$HOME/.local/bin/portly`, or the copy bundled with the app at `/Applications/Portly.app/Contents/Resources/portly-cli`.

## Inspect first

Run `portly status` for the compact active/problem view. Use `portly status --details` only when you need stopped servers, IDs, uptime, or resource metrics, and `portly status --json` when code needs structured fields. Use an exact server ID or `project/server` when names are ambiguous.

## Keep the project rules durable

Whenever setting up Portly for a repository, ensure its root `AGENTS.md` tells agents to use Portly for every persistent development server. Add the following rule if an equivalent rule is not already present; preserve all existing instructions and never duplicate it:

```md
## Development servers

- Always use Portly (`portly ...`) to start, stop, restart, inspect, or keep local development servers running.
- Start with `portly status`. Use `portly status --details` only for the full inventory and metrics, and `--json` only for machine-readable fields. Reuse a healthy managed server; if an in-scope server is running outside Portly, register it and use `portly take-over <project/server> --json`.
- For long-lived or reusable work, create a project and server.
- For builds, tests, code generation, previews, demos, and other bounded one-off work, run `job_id="$(portly temp '<command>' --path <folder> --timeout 30m)"`, then `portly wait "$job_id"`. `temp` returns immediately with an ID; `wait` prints captured logs and exits with the command's real code. A timeout kills the whole process group and exits with code `124`.
- Never launch persistent development servers directly, in the background, or through another supervisor.
```

The Portly installer also adds this rule, between `portly:managed-rule` markers, to `~/.agents/AGENTS.md` as a machine-wide fallback. Repository instructions remain useful for collaborators and environments that do not share that global file.

## Command reference

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `status`, `list`, `ls` | Compact active/problem view; add `--details` for the full inventory |
| `temp`, `temporary`, `run-temp` | Run a short-lived process outside any project |
| `wait` | Wait for a temporary job and return its real exit code |
| `action` | Run a configured maintenance action without restarting the server |
| `memory-limit`, `ram-limit` | Show or configure automatic project restarts by footprint |
| `start`, `stop`, `restart` | Control a server or every server in `--project` |
| `logs` | Read captured output with `--tail` |
| `add-project`, `add-server`, `update-server`, `remove` | Manage configuration |
| `take-over`, `adopt` | Move an external listener under Portly |
| `port`, `kill-port` | Inspect or explicitly stop a port occupant |
| `open`, `quit`, `config` | Control the app or read its configuration |
| `forever enable\|status\|disable` | Manage launch at login through the macOS LaunchAgent |

Run `portly <command> --help` for exact flags. Use `--json` when structured fields are actually needed; `config` prints JSON or a path directly.

## Choose project or temporary

- **Long-lived or reusable:** create or reuse a project, then add a named server. Projects persist across Portly launches and belong in the sidebar.
- **Small or one-off:** run `id=$(portly temp '<command>' --name <name> --path <folder> --timeout 30m)`, then `portly wait "$id"`. `temp` returns immediately; Portly supervises the whole background process group, captures logs and resource use, and kills it at the timeout. Completed metadata remains available for one hour but is never written to `config.json` or restored after relaunch.

Do not create a permanent project merely to host a build, test, quick preview, generated artifact, throwaway demo, or short verification server. A temporary job is still managed by Portly; never add shell backgrounding around it. Use `portly logs <id>` while it runs, `portly wait <id>` for its terminal result, and expect exit code `124` when its timeout is reached.

## Memory guard

Run `portly memory-limit` to inspect the effective policy. The global value is a default applied separately to every project, not a cap on all Portly processes combined. Configure it with `portly memory-limit 5GB` or disable it with `portly memory-limit off`.

Projects inherit the global value by default. Override one with `portly memory-limit 3GB --project <project>`, exempt it with `portly memory-limit off --project <project>`, or restore inheritance with `portly memory-limit inherit --project <project>`. `GB`, `Go`, `MB`, and `Mo` are accepted.

Portly evaluates total project footprint every two seconds. Three consecutive samples above the effective limit restart every running server in that project, then sampling starts fresh on the replacement processes. Configure these policies in Settings → Memory. Never enable or lower a memory limit without the user's authorization: changing it can restart active workloads.

## Add and verify a server

1. Confirm the project path and dev command from the repository.
2. Ensure the repository's root `AGENTS.md` contains the durable Portly rule above.
3. Register the project only if absent.
4. Check the intended port with `portly port <port> --json`.
5. Add it with `portly add-server --project <project> --name <name> --command '<command>' --port <port> --start --json`.
6. Poll `portly status --json` until `running` and `healthy`.
7. Verify the meaningful URL and inspect `portly logs <project/server> --tail 100 --json`.

Register projects with `portly add-project --name <name> --path <absolute-path> --icon <sf-symbol> --color '<hex>' --json`.

Portly injects `PORT`, `PORTLY=1`, and `PORTLY_SERVER`. The configured port drives health checks; a process that does not listen there will not become healthy.

## Operate and diagnose

Use `start`, `stop`, or `restart` with a server, or `--project <project>`. `portly stop --all --json` stops everything. Use `update-server` to change fields, then restart a running server.

For repeatable maintenance that must not restart the managed server, configure an action and run it as a supervised temporary job:

```bash
portly update-server <project/server> --action 'clear-cache=trash .next/cache'
job_id="$(portly action <project/server> clear-cache)"
portly wait "$job_id"
```

Actions inherit the server's working directory, environment, `PORT`, and original `PORTLY_SERVER`. Use an application endpoint or another framework-supported command for in-memory caches; removing a disk cache cannot clear state already held by the live process.

Inspect conflicts with `portly port <port> --json`. Use `portly kill-port <port> --json` only when the stop is requested or the occupant is confirmed in scope. Portly sends SIGTERM to regular processes and, for a Docker-published port, resolves and stops only the publishing container. It never auto-stops conflicts or signals Docker Desktop's global backend.

When a configured server's port is held by a process launched elsewhere, use `portly take-over <project/server> --json` (alias: `adopt`). Portly safely stops the process or publishing Docker container, waits for the port to be released, then starts the configured command itself. Never take over an unknown workload without confirming it is in scope.

Keep proof distinct: `status` proves Portly state, `logs` proves captured child output, `port` proves a listener, and `curl` proves the meaningful route responds.

## Remove, quit, and configure

- Remove a server: `portly remove <project/server> --json`.
- Remove a project: `portly remove --project <project> --json`.
- Show config: `portly config` or `portly config --path-only`.
- Open the app: `portly open --json`.
- Quit: `portly quit --json`.

Removing a project stops its servers. Quitting stops every managed server because Portly is the supervisor. The source of truth is `~/.config/portly/config.json`, hot-reloaded by the app; logs are in `~/.config/portly/logs/`.

## macOS forever mode

Use `portly forever enable --json` when Portly itself must launch at every macOS login. The command transfers currently active servers to the launchd-owned app. Verify both `portly forever status --json` and `portly status --json`; launchd state alone does not prove a managed server or its meaningful route works.

Use `portly forever disable --json` to unload the LaunchAgent recoverably while keeping currently active servers under a regular Portly launch.

## Linux

On Linux, use the headless `portly` binary from this repository's `cli/` folder. It is the supervisor: commands auto-start a loopback daemon and speak the same API as macOS. Do not install `Portly.app`. `open` has no window and reports that. `forever` uses a systemd user unit, not launchd; it errors clearly when systemd is missing. Do not run the macOS app and the Linux daemon against the same `7737` port.

args.prompt:
You are writing realistic seed data for a local Gmail-style email client (Vite + React + TypeScript). Work ONLY inside /private/var/folders/7z/5mtgxwxx4zs9ppgzm942gbmh0000gn/T/cursor-continuation-6ew_nafw/app . Do not read, list or touch anything outside that directory. Never use npm (pnpm only, and you should not need to install anything). Do not delete files.

## Read first
- `src/data/types.ts` — defines the seed authoring types you MUST use: `SeedThread`, `SeedMessage`, `SeedAttachment`, `SeedDraft`, `Contact`, `Ago`. Do not modify it.
- `src/data/contacts.ts` — existing contacts keyed by short camelCase keys (e.g. `sam`, `nora`, `mom`, `dad`, `jules`, `leah`, `tomas`, `gary`, `dentist`, `owen`, `rita`, `priya`, `maya`, `devon`...). Do not modify it.
- `src/data/seedThreads.ts` — already contains 28 high-quality WORK threads (read a few to match the tone, format and quality bar). Do not modify it.

## Your task: create ONE new file `src/data/seedPersonal.ts`
```ts
import type { Contact, SeedDraft, SeedThread } from './types';
export const PERSONAL_CONTACTS: Record<string, Contact> = { /* only NEW contacts you need; keys must not collide with contacts.ts keys */ };
export const PERSONAL: SeedThread[] = [ ... ];
export const SEED_DRAFTS: SeedDraft[] = [ ... ];
```
Contact references in `from`/`to`/`cc` are keys of contacts.ts or PERSONAL_CONTACTS, or the literal "me". Prefix any new keys with `p_` (e.g. `p_vet`) to guarantee no collisions. Keep new contacts to a minimum (0–6), `kind: 'person'` or `'brand'`.

## The mailbox owner
"me" = Robin Hale <robin.hale@fernbrook.co>, Design Lead at Fernbrook, a 25-person product design & engineering studio in Portland, OR. Partner: Sam Okafor (`sam`). Sister: Nora Hale (`nora`). Parents: Ellen (`mom`) and Richard (`dad`) Hale. Friends: Jules Moreau (`jules`, freelance designer), Leah Brooks (`leah`), Tomás Rivera (`tomas`). Landlord: Gary Lindgren (`gary`). Dentist: `dentist`. Running club organiser Owen Pryce (`owen`, Rose City Striders). CPA: Rita Gomez (`rita`).
Existing work context you may reference for consistency: Q4 roadmap (Atlas design system v2, Harbor Health patient portal Phase 2, Juniper Bank onboarding revamp), a fall team offsite at Silver Fir Lodge (~2-3 weeks out), a Denver workshop with Juniper Bank next week, Robin speaking at Tessellate Conf in spring, hiring for a Senior Product Designer.

## Time
"Today" is Tuesday, September 29, 2026 in Portland. `at` values are relative Ago strings: "12m", "3h", "2d@14:05" (2 days ago at 14:05 local), "40d@09:30". Regex: /^(\d+m|\d+h|\d+d@\d{2}:\d{2})$/ (always two-digit hours, e.g. "3d@08:05"). 1d = Monday, 2d = Sunday, 3d = Saturday, 8d = Monday, 9d = Sunday, 10d = Saturday, etc. Personal mail skews evenings and weekends. Messages in a thread must be chronological, oldest first. Never mention exact calendar dates — use "Thursday", "next weekend", "end of October", "Thanksgiving".

## PERSONAL threads — write 26 to 30 threads
Unique ids like "t-thanksgiving". Mix and requirements:
- Must include (multi-message, genuine back-and-forth with "me" replies):
  1. Thanksgiving planning with Nora and mom (and dad chiming in) — 5–7 messages, label "personal", the latest message unread and recent (e.g. "1h" or "3h").
  2. Sam and Robin planning a weekend trip to the Oregon coast (label "travel", maybe "personal") — 4–6 messages, with a cabin booking detail, one attachment (e.g. "cabin-confirmation.pdf" with a `preview`).
  3. Lease renewal with the landlord Gary — 3–4 messages, attachment "Lease-Renewal-2027.pdf" with a realistic `preview` (4–10 lines of plain text with \n), labels "personal","finance".
  4. Jules asking Robin for a portfolio review — 3–4 messages, attachment "Jules-Moreau-Portfolio-2026.pdf" (with preview), Robin gives thoughtful specific feedback in one message (150–250 words, with "- " bullets).
  5. Running club 10K logistics with Owen (Robin volunteering at a water station / pacing) — 3–5 messages, cc another runner if you want.
  6. Mom sending garden/dog photos: 2 image attachments like "IMG_4821.jpg" 3_204_551 bytes and "IMG_4822.jpg" (no preview for images), warm tone.
  7. Rita the CPA about Q3 estimated tax payment — labels "finance", attachment "2026-Q3-estimate-worksheet.pdf" or ".xlsx" with preview.
  8. Leah — dinner / birthday plans for Sam (surprise party planning), 3–4 messages, a few emojis OK.
  9. Tomás — borrowing camping gear or a record-player repair or a band gig; casual.
  10. Dad forwarding an article or asking a tech-support question (subject starting "Fwd:" is fine).
  11. A voice memo from Sam (attachment "voice-memo.m4a" ~ 412_000 bytes), short body.
- Sent-only threads: 8 threads with `location: 'sent'`, where the only message(s) are from "me" (no reply from others). Mix personal and work, e.g. Robin to Gary (maintenance request: dishwasher), Robin to Rita (documents attached: "1099-NEC-Fernbrook.pdf"), Robin to Devon (comments on the Atlas token naming RFC), Robin to Mira at Tessellate (travel details for the spring talk), Robin to Owen (volunteering sign-up), Robin to Nora (recipe), Robin to Hannah Ortiz (`hannah`) sending signed panel pricing, Robin to `designTeam` (weekly design notes). At least 3 of these should be within the last 7 days; 2 should have attachments.
- Trash: 2 threads with `location: 'trash'` (e.g. an old group-chat style thread, an outdated plan).
- Archive: 4 threads with `location: 'archive'` (older, resolved).
- Snoozed: exactly 1 inbox thread with `snoozeHours: 5` (e.g. Leah's book club pick).
- Unread: 7–9 threads `unread: true`, all in the inbox and most within the last 2 days (a couple at "25m", "1h", "5h").
- Starred: 3–4 threads. Important: 3–4 threads.
- All personal threads use `category: 'primary'`, except: dentist appointment reminder (category 'updates', from `dentist`, 1 message, include it) — so there are 12+ single-message threads too.
- Time distribution: ~5 within the last 12h ("Nm"/"Nh"), ~10 within 1–7 days, the rest 8–200 days, 2 older than 270 days (e.g. last year's Thanksgiving recap photos, or a trip).
- Labels: only "work", "personal", "travel", "finance", "receipts", "clients". About half the threads carry 1–2 labels.
- Bodies: plain-text `body` only (no html). Natural, specific, varied length (1 line to ~250 words), distinct voices (warm mom with a bit of rambling, dry dad, chatty Leah, terse Sam texts-as-email, precise Rita). Blank lines between paragraphs, "- " bullets where natural, sign-offs for longer notes, occasional fictional URLs (https://...). Replies must NOT include quoted history — just the new text. Use template literals (backticks) for bodies like seedThreads.ts does. No lorem ipsum, no placeholders, no real companies or real people. Real places (Portland, Oregon coast towns, Mt. Hood) are fine.
- Attachments: realistic names and byte sizes; documents (pdf/docx/xlsx/pptx) must include a `preview` plain-text excerpt (4–12 lines, "\n" separated) that reads like the first page.

## SEED_DRAFTS — exactly 4
- Two new-message drafts (unfinished, realistic — e.g. an email to Nora half-written, a note to `hannah` or `owen`).
- One reply draft with `threadId: 't-tidewater-questions'` (an existing work thread; Jess Calloway `jess` asked questions about Fernbrook's proposal), `to: ['jess']`, a partially written answer; subject can be the base subject.
- One scheduled draft with `scheduleInHours: 24`, e.g. a note to `designTeam` about tomorrow's crit agenda. Subject + body complete.
`at` = when the draft was last edited (e.g. "35m", "2h", "1d@21:40").

## Validation (must pass before you finish)
1. Write a temporary check script at `scripts/check-personal.ts` that imports `../src/data/contacts.ts` and `../src/data/seedPersonal.ts` (explicit .ts extensions) and verifies: every contact key used exists in CONTACTS or PERSONAL_CONTACTS (or is "me"); no PERSONAL_CONTACTS key collides with CONTACTS; ids unique and none collide with ids in `../src/data/seedThreads.ts` (you can regex-scan that file's text with fs for `id: '...'`); each thread has ≥1 message; label ids are in the allowed set; every `at` matches the regex; messages chronological within each thread (convert to approximate minutes-ago: Nm→N, Nh→N*60, Nd@HH:MM→N*1440-(HH*60+MM)+1440 … any monotonic approximation is fine; must be non-increasing); `location: 'sent'` threads contain only messages from "me"; the draft threadId is 't-tidewater-questions'. Print counts by location/unread/starred/attachments. Run it with `node --experimental-strip-types scripts/check-personal.ts`. Fix every problem.
2. Run `./node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit -p .` from the app root. Other files in the project are being written concurrently by another engineer and may have errors — only make sure `src/data/seedPersonal.ts` has none (filter the output for your file name).
3. Leave the check script in place.

Report back briefly: file path, thread count, counts per location / unread / starred / with attachments, any new PERSONAL_CONTACTS keys, and anything notable.

Regex: /^(\d+m|\d+h|\d+d@\d{2}:\d{2})$/ (always two-digit hours, e.g. "3d@08:05"). 1d = Monday, 2d = Sunday, 3d = Saturday, 8d = Monday, 9d = Sunday, 10d = Saturday, etc. Personal mail skews evenings and weekends. Messages in a thread must be chronological, oldest first. Never mention exact calendar dates — use "Thursday", "next weekend", "end of October", "Thanksgiving".

## PERSONAL threads — write 26 to 30 threads
Unique ids like "t-thanksgiving". Mix and requirements:
- Must include (multi-message, genuine back-and-forth with "me" replies):
  1. Thanksgiving planning with Nora and mom (and dad chiming in) — 5–7 messages, label "personal", the latest message unread and recent (e.g. "1h" or "3h").
  2. Sam and Robin planning a weekend trip to the Oregon coast (label "travel", maybe "personal") — 4–6 messages, with a cabin booking detail, one attachment (e.g. "cabin-confirmation.pdf" with a `preview`).
  3. Lease renewal with the landlord Gary — 3–4 messages, attachment "Lease-Renewal-2027.pdf" with a realistic `preview` (4–10 lines of plain text with \n), labels "personal","finance".
  4. Jules asking Robin for a portfolio review — 3–4 messages, attachment "Jules-Moreau-Portfolio-2026.pdf" (with preview), Robin gives thoughtful specific feedback in one message (150–250 words, with "- " bullets).
  5. Running club 10K logistics with Owen (Robin volunteering at a water station / pacing) — 3–5 messages, cc another runner if you want.
  6. Mom sending garden/dog photos: 2 image attachments like "IMG_4821.jpg" 3_204_551 bytes and "IMG_4822.jpg" (no preview for images), warm tone.
  7. Rita the CPA about Q3 estimated tax payment — labels "finance", attachment "2026-Q3-estimate-worksheet.pdf" or ".xlsx" with preview.
  8. Leah — dinner / birthday plans for Sam (surprise party planning), 3–4 messages, a few emojis OK.
  9. Tomás — borrowing camping gear or a record-player repair or a band gig; casual.
  10. Dad forwarding an article or asking a tech-support question (subject starting "Fwd:" is fine).
  11. A voice memo from Sam (attachment "voice-memo.m4a" ~ 412_000 bytes), short body.
- Sent-only threads: 8 threads with `location: 'sent'`, where the only message(s) are from "me" (no reply from others). Mix personal and work, e.g. Robin to Gary (maintenance request: dishwasher), Robin to Rita (documents attached: "1099-NEC-Fernbrook.pdf"), Robin to Devon (comments on the Atlas token naming RFC), Robin to Mira at Tessellate (travel details for the spring talk), Robin to Owen (volunteering sign-up), Robin to Nora (recipe), Robin to Hannah Ortiz (`hannah`) sending signed panel pricing, Robin to `designTeam` (weekly design notes). At least 3 of these should be within the last 7 days; 2 should have attachments.
- Trash: 2 threads with `location: 'trash'` (e.g. an old group-chat style thread, an outdated plan).
- Archive: 4 threads with `location: 'archive'` (older, resolved).
- Snoozed: exactly 1 inbox thread with `snoozeHours: 5` (e.g. Leah's book club pick).
- Unread: 7–9 threads `unread: true`, all in the inbox and most within the last 2 days (a couple at "25m", "1h", "5h").
- Starred: 3–4 threads. Important: 3–4 threads.
- All personal threads use `category: 'primary'`, except: dentist appointment reminder (category 'updates', from `dentist`, 1 message, include it) — so there are 12+ single-message threads too.
- Time distribution: ~5 within the last 12h ("Nm"/"Nh"), ~10 within 1–7 days, the rest 8–200 days, 2 older than 270 days (e.g. last year's Thanksgiving recap photos, or a trip).
- Labels: only "work", "personal", "travel", "finance", "receipts", "clients". About half the threads carry 1–2 labels.
- Bodies: plain-text `body` only (no html). Natural, specific, varied length (1 line to ~250 words), distinct voices (warm mom with a bit of rambling, dry dad, chatty Leah, terse Sam texts-as-email, precise Rita). Blank lines between paragraphs, "- " bullets where natural, sign-offs for longer notes, occasional fictional URLs (https://...). Replies must NOT include quoted history — just the new text. Use template literals (backticks) for bodies like seedThreads.ts does. No lorem ipsum, no placeholders, no real companies or real people. Real places (Portland, Oregon coast towns, Mt. Hood) are fine.
- Attachments: realistic names and byte sizes; documents (pdf/docx/xlsx/pptx) must include a `preview` plain-text excerpt (4–12 lines, "\n" separated) that reads like the first page.

## SEED_DRAFTS — exactly 4
- Two new-message drafts (unfinished, realistic — e.g. an email to Nora half-written, a note to `hannah` or `owen`).
- One reply draft with `threadId: 't-tidewater-questions'` (an existing work thread; Jess Calloway `jess` asked questions about Fernbrook's proposal), `to: ['jess']`, a partially written answer; subject can be the base subject.
- One scheduled draft with `scheduleInHours: 24`, e.g. a note to `designTeam` about tomorrow's crit agenda. Subject + body complete.
`at` = when the draft was last edited (e.g. "35m", "2h", "1d@21:40").

## Validation (must pass before you finish)
1. Write a temporary check script at `scripts/check-personal.ts` that imports `../src/data/contacts.ts` and `../src/data/seedPersonal.ts` (explicit .ts extensions) and verifies: every contact key used exists in CONTACTS or PERSONAL_CONTACTS (or is "me"); no PERSONAL_CONTACTS key collides with CONTACTS; ids unique and none collide with ids in `../src/data/seedThreads.ts` (you can regex-scan that file's text with fs for `id: '...'`); each thread has ≥1 message; label ids are in the allowed set; every `at` matches the regex; messages chronological within each thread (convert to approximate minutes-ago: Nm→N, Nh→N*60, Nd@HH:MM→N*1440-(HH*60+MM)+1440 … any monotonic approximation is fine; must be non-increasing); `location: 'sent'` threads contain only messages from "me"; the draft threadId is 't-tidewater-questions'. Print counts by location/unread/starred/attachments. Run it with `node --experimental-strip-types scripts/check-personal.ts`. Fix every problem.
2. Run `./node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit -p .` from the app root. Other files in the project are being written concurrently by another engineer and may have errors — only make sure `src/data/seedPersonal.ts` has none (filter the output for your file name).
3. Leave the check script in place.

Report back briefly: file path, thread count, counts per location / unread / starred / with attachments, any new PERSONAL_CONTACTS keys, and anything notable.

import type { SeedThread, SeedDraft } from './types';

/*
 * Seed mailbox for Robin Hale, Design Lead at Fernbrook (Portland, OR).
 * Timestamps are relative ("25m", "3h", "4d@10:15") and resolved when the mailbox is first created.
 * The content assumes "today" is a Tuesday in late September, so 2d/3d, 9d/10d, 16d/17d … are weekend days.
 */

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
/* Work — Fernbrook, clients and vendors                               */
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */

const WORK: SeedThread[] = [
  {
    id: 't-roadmap-q4',
    subject: 'Q4 roadmap — Atlas, Harbor Phase 2, Juniper',
    category: 'primary',
    labels: ['work'],
    starred: true,
    important: true,
    unread: true,
    messages: [
      {
        from: 'priya',
        to: ['maya', 'devon', 'aisha', 'me'],
        at: '6d@09:12',
        body: `Hi all,

Attached is v2 of the Q4 roadmap. I'd like us to lock this by the end of next week so we can share it with the whole team before the offsite.

Four themes, in rough priority order:
- Atlas v2.0 (tokens, dark mode, docs relaunch)
- Harbor patient portal Phase 2
- Juniper onboarding revamp
- Tidewater discovery, if they sign

I know this is more than we can comfortably do. Please reply with where you think it breaks — be specific about people and weeks, not vibes.

Priya`,
        attachments: [
          {
            name: 'Q4-roadmap-v2.pdf',
            size: 2_311_870,
            preview: `Fernbrook — Q4 Roadmap (DRAFT v2)
Owner: Priya Raman · Status: for discussion

1. Atlas design system v2.0
   - OKLCH color tokens, dark mode, docs site relaunch
2. Harbor patient portal — Phase 2
   - Appointments, secure messaging, WCAG 2.2 AA audit
3. Juniper onboarding revamp
   - Research synthesis, prototypes, pilot readiness
4. Tidewater Outfitters (pending signature)
   - Discovery sprint`,
          },
        ],
      },
      {
        from: 'devon',
        to: ['priya'],
        cc: ['maya', 'aisha', 'me'],
        at: '6d@10:41',
        body: `Where it breaks: engineering is ~18% over in Oct/Nov on this plan. Capacity sheet attached.

Biggest single item is Atlas dark mode — it touches every component and needs a full visual regression pass. If that moves to Q1 we're roughly even.

Also flagging that Ines is on-call for Harbor through November, so she's at ~75%.`,
        attachments: [
          {
            name: 'eng-capacity-q4.xlsx',
            size: 48_902,
            preview: `Engineering capacity — Q4 (person-weeks)

Team member   | Oct | Nov | Dec | Notes
Devon Price   |  3  |  4  |  3  | lead, 50% mgmt
Marcus Bell   |  4  |  4  |  3  | Atlas
Ines Duarte   |  4  |  3  |  3  | Harbor on-call
(+3 others)   | 12  | 12  |  9  | holidays in Dec
Total         | 23  | 23  | 18  |
Demand (v2)   | 27  | 27  | 21  | over by ~17%`,
          },
        ],
      },
      {
        from: 'me',
        to: ['priya'],
        cc: ['maya', 'devon', 'aisha'],
        at: '6d@13:05',
        body: `Same story on design. With Theo, Lena and Kai (plus a senior hire in November if the offer we're about to make lands), we can realistically carry three streams, not four.

My proposal:
- Keep Atlas v2.0 tokens + docs site in Q4, move dark mode to Q1
- Harbor Phase 2 gets Theo full-time and Kai at 50%
- Juniper gets Lena full-time; I'll co-run research synthesis with Aisha
- Tidewater discovery only if they sign before November — and then I lead it myself

Dark mode is the thing I most want to do, so it hurts to say this, but it's the right call.

Robin`,
      },
      {
        from: 'aisha',
        to: ['me', 'priya'],
        cc: ['maya', 'devon'],
        at: '5d@08:52',
        body: `+1 to Robin's split. One caveat from the Juniper side: Grace's team wants clickable prototypes before their pilot go/no-go in mid-November, so Lena's time can't get borrowed for Harbor fire drills. If that's a risk I'd rather know now.

Happy to co-run synthesis — I've already tagged about half of the session notes in Driftbox.`,
      },
      {
        from: 'maya',
        to: ['priya', 'me'],
        cc: ['devon', 'aisha'],
        at: '5d@11:20',
        body: `Agree with moving dark mode. For Harbor, the WCAG 2.2 AA audit is written into the Phase 2 SOW, so it has to land in Q4 — Rachel asked about it on our last call too.

Theo + half of Kai works for me as long as Kai's time is protected on Tuesdays and Thursdays, when we sit with Ben's clinical team.`,
      },
      {
        from: 'priya',
        to: ['maya', 'devon', 'aisha', 'me'],
        at: '4d@10:15',
        body: `Thanks — this is exactly the conversation I wanted. Decisions:

1. Atlas dark mode moves to Q1. Atlas v2.0 tokens and the docs site stay in Q4.
2. Design staffing per Robin's note, with Maya's Tue/Thu constraint for Kai.
3. Tidewater discovery is contingent on signature; Robin leads if it happens.

Maya, can you fold this into v3? I'll review Monday.`,
      },
      {
        from: 'maya',
        to: ['priya'],

---
name: portly
description: Manage persistent projects and temporary local processes with the Portly macOS app and CLI. Use when an agent needs to run, start, stop, restart, inspect logs or health, configure projects and ports, adopt external listeners, resolve port conflicts, or enable launch at login.
---

# Portly

Use the `portly` CLI as the primary interface. Every command launches Portly.app automatically if needed; this is a state-changing side effect even for `status` when the app was closed.

If `portly` is not available on `PATH`, use the onboarding-installed CLI at `$HOME/.local/bin/portly`, or the copy bundled with the app at `/Applications/Portly.app/Contents/Resources/portly-cli`.

## Inspect first

Run `portly status` for the compact active/problem view. Use `portly status --details` only when you need stopped servers, IDs, uptime, or resource metrics, and `portly status --json` when code needs structured fields. Use an exact server ID or `project/server` when names are ambiguous.

## Keep the project rules durable

Whenever setting up Portly for a repository, ensure its root `AGENTS.md` tells agents to use Portly for every persistent development server. Add the following rule if an equivalent rule is not already present; preserve all existing instructions and never duplicate it:

```md
## Development servers

- Always use Portly (`portly ...`) to start, stop, restart, inspect, or keep local development servers running.
- Start with `portly status`. Use `portly status --details` only for the full inventory and metrics, and `--json` only for machine-readable fields. Reuse a healthy managed server; if an in-scope server is running outside Portly, register it and use `portly take-over <project/server> --json`.
- For long-lived or reusable work, create a project and server.
- For builds, tests, code generation, previews, demos, and other bounded one-off work, run `job_id="$(portly temp '<command>' --path <folder> --timeout 30m)"`, then `portly wait "$job_id"`. `temp` returns immediately with an ID; `wait` prints captured logs and exits with the command's real code. A timeout kills the whole process group and exits with code `124`.
- Never launch persistent development servers directly, in the background, or through another supervisor.
```

The Portly installer also adds this rule, between `portly:managed-rule` markers, to `~/.agents/AGENTS.md` as a machine-wide fallback. Repository instructions remain useful for collaborators and environments that do not share that global file.

## Command reference

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `status`, `list`, `ls` | Compact active/problem view; add `--details` for the full inventory |
| `temp`, `temporary`, `run-temp` | Run a short-lived process outside any project |
| `wait` | Wait for a temporary job and return its real exit code |
| `action` | Run a configured maintenance action without restarting the server |
| `memory-limit`, `ram-limit` | Show or configure automatic project restarts by footprint |
| `start`, `stop`, `restart` | Control a server or every server in `--project` |
| `logs` | Read captured output with `--tail` |
| `add-project`, `add-server`, `update-server`, `remove` | Manage configuration |
| `take-over`, `adopt` | Move an external listener under Portly |
| `port`, `kill-port` | Inspect or explicitly stop a port occupant |
| `open`, `quit`, `config` | Control the app or read its configuration |
| `forever enable\|status\|disable` | Manage launch at login through the macOS LaunchAgent |

Run `portly <command> --help` for exact flags. Use `--json` when structured fields are actually needed; `config` prints JSON or a path directly.

## Choose project or temporary

- **Long-lived or reusable:** create or reuse a project, then add a named server. Projects persist across Portly launches and belong in the sidebar.
- **Small or one-off:** run `id=$(portly temp '<command>' --name <name> --path <folder> --timeout 30m)`, then `portly wait "$id"`. `temp` returns immediately; Portly supervises the whole background process group, captures logs and resource use, and kills it at the timeout. Completed metadata remains available for one hour but is never written to `config.json` or restored after relaunch.

Do not create a permanent project merely to host a build, test, quick preview, generated artifact, throwaway demo, or short verification server. A temporary job is still managed by Portly; never add shell backgrounding around it. Use `portly logs <id>` while it runs, `portly wait <id>` for its terminal result, and expect exit code `124` when its timeout is reached.

## Memory guard

Run `portly memory-limit` to inspect the effective policy. The global value is a default applied separately to every project, not a cap on all Portly processes combined. Configure it with `portly memory-limit 5GB` or disable it with `portly memory-limit off`.

Projects inherit the global value by default. Override one with `portly memory-limit 3GB --project <project>`, exempt it with `portly memory-limit off --project <project>`, or restore inheritance with `portly memory-limit inherit --project <project>`. `GB`, `Go`, `MB`, and `Mo` are accepted.

Portly evaluates total project footprint every two seconds. Three consecutive samples above the effective limit restart every running server in that project, then sampling starts fresh on the replacement processes. Configure these policies in Settings → Memory. Never enable or lower a memory limit without the user's authorization: changing it can restart active workloads.

## Add and verify a server

1. Confirm the project path and dev command from the repository.
2. Ensure the repository's root `AGENTS.md` contains the durable Portly rule above.
3. Register the project only if absent.
4. Check the intended port with `portly port <port> --json`.
5. Add it with `portly add-server --project <project> --name <name> --command '<command>' --port <port> --start --json`.
6. Poll `portly status --json` until `running` and `healthy`.
7. Verify the meaningful URL and inspect `portly logs <project/server> --tail 100 --json`.

Register projects with `portly add-project --name <name> --path <absolute-path> --icon <sf-symbol> --color '<hex>' --json`.

Portly injects `PORT`, `PORTLY=1`, and `PORTLY_SERVER`. The configured port drives health checks; a process that does not listen there will not become healthy.

## Operate and diagnose

Use `start`, `stop`, or `restart` with a server, or `--project <project>`. `portly stop --all --json` stops everything. Use `update-server` to change fields, then restart a running server.

For repeatable maintenance that must not restart the managed server, configure an action and run it as a supervised temporary job:

```bash
portly update-server <project/server> --action 'clear-cache=trash .next/cache'
job_id="$(portly action <project/server> clear-cache)"
portly wait "$job_id"
```

Actions inherit the server's working directory, environment, `PORT`, and original `PORTLY_SERVER`. Use an application endpoint or another framework-supported command for in-memory caches; removing a disk cache cannot clear state already held by the live process.

Inspect conflicts with `portly port <port> --json`. Use `portly kill-port <port> --json` only when the stop is requested or the occupant is confirmed in scope. Portly sends SIGTERM to regular processes and, for a Docker-published port, resolves and stops only the publishing container. It never auto-stops conflicts or signals Docker Desktop's global backend.

When a configured server's port is held by a process launched elsewhere, use `portly take-over <project/server> --json` (alias: `adopt`). Portly safely stops the process or publishing Docker container, waits for the port to be released, then starts the configured command itself. Never take over an unknown workload without confirming it is in scope.

Keep proof distinct: `status` proves Portly state, `logs` proves captured child output, `port` proves a listener, and `curl` proves the meaningful route responds.

## Remove, quit, and configure

- Remove a server: `portly remove <project/server> --json`.
- Remove a project: `portly remove --project <project> --json`.
- Show config: `portly config` or `portly config --path-only`.
- Open the app: `portly open --json`.
- Quit: `portly quit --json`.

Removing a project stops its servers. Quitting stops every managed server because Portly is the supervisor. The source of truth is `~/.config/portly/config.json`, hot-reloaded by the app; logs are in `~/.config/portly/logs/`.

## macOS forever mode

Use `portly forever enable --json` when Portly itself must launch at every macOS login. The command transfers currently active servers to the launchd-owned app. Verify both `portly forever status --json` and `portly status --json`; launchd state alone does not prove a managed server or its meaningful route works.

Use `portly forever disable --json` to unload the LaunchAgent recoverably while keeping currently active servers under a regular Portly launch.

## Linux

On Linux, use the headless `portly` binary from this repository's `cli/` folder. It is the supervisor: commands auto-start a loopback daemon and speak the same API as macOS. Do not install `Portly.app`. `open` has no window and reports that. `forever` uses a systemd user unit, not launchd; it errors clearly when systemd is missing. Do not run the macOS app and the Linux daemon against the same `7737` port.

---
name: dev-browser
description: Browser automation with persistent page state using the dev-browser CLI. Use when the user mentions browse, open website, click, fill form, screenshot, scrape, automate browser, test website, log into, navigate, web page, or any browser interaction.
allowed-tools:
  - Bash(dev-browser *)
  - Bash(/Applications/Helium.app/Contents/MacOS/Helium *)
---

Drive every browser task with the `dev-browser` CLI. Never use Cursor IDE Browser MCP (`cursor-ide-browser`, `browser_navigate`, `browser_snapshot`, `browser_lock`, `browser_click`, `browser_cdp`, or any `browser_*` tool).

If `dev-browser` is missing: obey the repo's package-manager rules (no `npm install -g` when npm is forbidden). In Codex, prefer the bundled Node/Playwright/Chromium runtime for page-load, screenshot, console, and interaction checks. Install the CLI only when npm is allowed and the task needs persistence or CDP the bundled runtime cannot provide: `npm install -g dev-browser && dev-browser install`. When falling back to Playwright, keep the same proof (URL, title, errors, screenshots, exact steps) and state that the CLI was unavailable.

Write one-thing scripts. Reuse named pages (`browser.getPage("main")`) across runs. End each script by logging JSON state. Commands, flags, Page methods, locators, screenshots, forms, and CDP connect: [api-reference.md](references/api-reference.md). Open that file before inventing a Page method.

File I/O is only `~/.dev-browser/tmp/`. Never pass absolute paths to `saveScreenshot` or `writeFile`; copy out from the returned tmp path.

Helium is not auto-discovered. Launch it with `--remote-debugging-port` and connect with `dev-browser --browser helium --connect http://127.0.0.1:<port>`. An already-running Helium without CDP cannot be attached; if it must not restart, use AppleScript or Computer Use.

On script failure, the page stays put. Reconnect, screenshot, log URL/title, then continue.

# dev-browser API Reference

## Playwright Page Methods

Pages returned by `browser.getPage()` and `browser.newPage()` are full Playwright Page objects.
Full docs: https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-page

### Navigation

| Method | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `page.goto(url)` | Navigate to URL |
| `page.goBack()` | Go back |
| `page.goForward()` | Go forward |
| `page.reload()` | Reload page |
| `page.waitForURL(pattern)` | Wait for navigation (supports glob: `**/success`) |

### Element Interaction

| Method | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `page.click(selector)` | Click element |
| `page.fill(selector, value)` | Fill input field |
| `page.type(selector, text)` | Type text character by character |
| `page.press(selector, key)` | Press key (Enter, Tab, etc.) |
| `page.check(selector)` | Check checkbox |
| `page.uncheck(selector)` | Uncheck checkbox |
| `page.selectOption(selector, value)` | Select dropdown option |

### Locators (preferred for role-based targeting)

| Method | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `page.getByRole(role, { name })` | Target by ARIA role |
| `page.getByText(text)` | Target by text content |
| `page.getByLabel(label)` | Target by label |
| `page.getByPlaceholder(text)` | Target by placeholder |
| `page.getByTestId(id)` | Target by test ID |
| `page.locator(selector)` | Create locator for chained actions |

### Content Extraction

| Method | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `page.title()` | Get page title |
| `page.url()` | Get current URL |
| `page.textContent(selector)` | Get text content of element |
| `page.innerHTML(selector)` | Get inner HTML of element |
| `page.evaluate(fn)` | Run JavaScript in page context (plain JS only) |
| `page.$$eval(selector, fn)` | Run function on all matching elements |
| `page.$eval(selector, fn)` | Run function on first matching element |

### Waiting

| Method | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `page.waitForSelector(selector)` | Wait for element to appear |
| `page.waitForURL(url)` | Wait for navigation to URL |
| `page.waitForLoadState(state)` | Wait for load state (`load`, `domcontentloaded`, `networkidle`) |
| `page.waitForTimeout(ms)` | Wait for specified milliseconds |

### Screenshots & Visual

| Method | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `page.screenshot()` | Capture screenshot buffer |
| `page.screenshot({ fullPage: true })` | Full page screenshot |
| `page.screenshot({ path: "file.png" })` | Save screenshot to path |

### AI Snapshots

```javascript
const result = await page.snapshotForAI(options);
// Returns: { full: string, incremental?: string }
// Options: { track?: string, depth?: number, timeout?: number }
```

- Use `snapshotForAI()` to discover page structure before interacting
- Use `snapshotForAI({ track: "name" })` after page changes to get incremental diff
- Read `result.full` to identify elements, then use Playwright selectors to interact

## Sandbox Globals

Available in every script (NOT Node.js):

| Global | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `browser` | Pre-connected browser handle |
| `console` | log, warn, error, info (routed to CLI output) |
| `setTimeout` / `clearTimeout` | Basic timers |
| `saveScreenshot(buf, name)` | Save screenshot buffer (async) |
| `writeFile(name, data)` | Write file to temp dir (async) |
| `readFile(name)` | Read file from temp dir (async) |

**NOT available**: `require()`, `import()`, `process`, `fs`, `path`, `os`, `fetch`, `WebSocket`, `__dirname`, `__filename`

## CLI Commands

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `dev-browser run <file>` | Run a script file |
| `dev-browser install` | Install Playwright browsers (Chromium) |
| `dev-browser install-skill` | Install skill into agent directories |
| `dev-browser browsers` | List managed browser instances |
| `dev-browser status` | Show daemon status |
| `dev-browser stop` | Stop daemon and all browsers |

## Invocation Styles

```bash
# Heredoc (most common)
dev-browser <<'EOF'
const page = await browser.getPage("main");
EOF

# Script file
dev-browser run script.js

# Pipe
dev-browser --browser my-project < script.js

# Connect to external Chrome
dev-browser --connect http://localhost:9222 <<'EOF'
const page = await browser.getPage("main");
EOF

# Auto-discover Chrome
dev-browser --connect <<'EOF'
const page = await browser.getPage("main");
EOF
```
